issues.on_page: Cash 174,356; Cash - restricted 4,074; Cash held by county treasurer 1,017; TOTAL ASSETS 179,447 (Total Governmental Funds; also p1 Governmental Activities)
issues.issue: Requested check. 179,447 is printed, but only as TOTAL ASSETS and never as a cash figure. No line labelled cash prints that amount; the printed cash lines are 174,356 (Cash), 4,074 (restricted) and 1,017 (county treasurer). The JSON marks it computed as a sum of those three lines. Under the 2026-11-06 ruling (cash is never derived), this is a derived cash figure. It also equals ending_fund_balance 179,447. Lyman_FY2022, which uses the same auditor format, leaves ending_cash null in this situation. The options are null, or the printed Cash line 174,356. A person should decide; Lynch FY2023 used the same approach and drew the same flag.

issues.on_page: Other 7,839 = General 2,670 + Street 585 + Housing 4,581 + Flood Disaster 3
issues.issue: Housing's 4,581 (58% of the line) is printed as Charges for services on p11 and counted in Charges for Services on p2 (Community improvement). Under the extractor's broad-line rule, a category over half of the line would apply. The extraction kept the line as other (the label decision) and raised a decision_needed entry, which is defensible.
The category (state aid) and detail_category (federal grants) disagree for one combined federal-plus-state line with no printed breakdown. Page 2 shows it as Capital Grants for Community improvement.
The row names its function (housing), so under the capital outlay rule the label would be 'Capital Outlay: Housing'.

issues.extracted: computed: counted in Charges for Services on the Statement of Activities (p2: Sewer 92,382)
issues.issue: The amount is printed as-is. The 'computed' field holds a category justification, so the line will look like a derived value. The category itself is supported (p2 Sewer charges 92,382 = 64,862 + 27,456 + 64).
